references.title: MDN: image file types and format selection

title: Choosing the right format for smaller web files
description: A practical guide to image formats, audio bitrate, video codecs and the limits of PDF optimization.
seoDescription: Choose JPG, PNG, WebP, MP3 or MP4 for your task. Understand transparency, lossy encoding, audio bitrate and PDF optimization limits.

body.text: Start with what your file needs to do: display a photograph, preserve a transparent logo, play a clip or keep a document readable. A smaller file is useful only when its format and quality still suit that job.

items: JPG/JPEG: a practical choice for photographs. Re-encoding is lossy, and JPEG cannot store transparency.

PNG: useful for screenshots, diagrams and transparent artwork. Maximum is the default and may reduce colors. Choose Lossless to preserve decoded pixels. Smart, Maximum and Target size may reduce colors while preserving transparency; visible color changes are possible. Original dimensions are kept unless you explicitly resize. Re-encoding can also normalize color or remove metadata.
WebP: supports transparency and can be useful for compact web images. FileCompresser offers JPG, PNG and WebP output for supported still images; compare the downloaded result before publishing.

body.caption: Choose a format for the job, then compare the actual output.

body.text: For constant-bitrate audio, approximate payload size is bitrate multiplied by duration, divided by eight. For example, 60 seconds at 128 kbps is about 960,000 bytes before container and tag overhead. This is arithmetic, not a FileCompresser benchmark. Actual encoded size can differ.

WAV-to-MP3 conversion can reduce uncompressed PCM audio substantially. Re-encoding an existing MP3 at a lower bitrate may save space but adds another lossy generation. Increasing bitrate cannot recover detail lost earlier.
Video: distinguish the container from the codec

MP4 and MOV describe containers, not a single video codec. FileCompresser accepts supported MP4/MOV inputs and re-encodes to H.264 video with AAC audio when an audio track is present. A smaller resolution cap can help, but high-motion scenes and long clips still take time and memory. Unsupported codecs fail rather than becoming playable just by changing the extension.

The PDF tool tries a structure rewrite with selected document metadata removed. It does not downsample scanned pages or recompress embedded photos. If the candidate is not smaller, the unchanged original is retained with its metadata. Detected digitally signed and encrypted documents are refused rather than silently rewritten.
Keep the result that suits your task

Check dimensions, transparency, text readability, playback and the reported output size. Ordinary compression retains the original if no smaller candidate is found. An explicit format conversion or resize can increase bytes, but growth is never described as a saving. Keep your source until you have verified the download.
